feedback.end: William Shakespeare is considered to be one of the world’s greatest playwrights — somebody who writes plays for the stage. Shakespeare’s plays are just as popular now as they were over 400 years ago!
Shakespeare’s life is clouded in mystery! Historians have struggled to piece together a clear picture of the playwright as he has no official portraits or personal diaries.

instruction.text: Let’s try to piece together Shakespeare’s mysterious life by using these clues. Find Shakespeare’s name on the scroll.

feedback.end: Shakespeare’s birth was recorded in April 1564. He was born to a wealthy family in the market town of Stratford-upon-Avon.

instruction.text: Select the strange writing on the paper.

end.text: This is written in Latin, which was the language used by the Romans. Shakespeare studied Latin alongside Ancient Greek at his local school. He refers to lots of Latin and Greek stories in his own plays.

atoms.a: Which writing tools do you think Shakespeare used in school?

feedback.end: Hornbooks were pieces of paper fixed onto a small wooden board with a handle. Shakespeare would have used one to learn to read and write at school.

instruction.text: Select the question mark on the timeline of Shakespeare’s youth.

end.text: 1585 to 1592 are known as “the lost years” of Shakespeare’s life. During this time, there is little historical evidence of what Shakespeare was getting up to! All we know is that by 1592 he had begun working as an actor and playwright in London’s theatres.
end.sound: fifteen-eighty-five to fifteen-ninety-two are known as “the lost years” of Shakespeare’s life. During this time, there is little historical evidence of what Shakespeare was getting up to! All we know is that by fifteen-ninety-two he had begun working as an actor and playwright in London’s theatres.

hint.text: A plague is a serious disease often spread by rats and their fleas.
hint.label: Plague

atoms.a: When plague broke out in 1593, what do you think happened to London’s theatres?

feedback.end: When the theatres closed in 1593, Shakespeare took a break from playwrighting and tried out writing poems — mainly about love. One of these poems was his first published work.
